confirmed.statement: S1 assigned 97 third-grade students aged 8?9 in central China: 48 in the chatbot class and 49 in the search-engine class. One of the two intact classes was randomly selected for the experimental condition; assignment was at class level.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Methods?Participants; p. 6, Fig. 1 (arm labels).

confirmed.statement: S1 analyzed 89 students with complete pre- and post-tests: 45 chatbot and 44 search-engine students. Table 5 uses these same arm counts for all four post-test score outcomes (S1-O1 through S1-O4).
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Data analysis, first paragraph; p. 13, Results RQ1 and Table 5, title and column headings.

confirmed.statement: The baseline analysis included 90 valid pre-test samples: 46 chatbot students and 44 search-engine students. Longitudinal comparisons used 45 and 44 paired student records, respectively.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Data analysis, first paragraph; p. 13, Results RQ1, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: Eight assigned students were absent from the complete-case test analysis: 48?45=3 in the chatbot arm and 49?44=5 in the search arm (derived by subtraction). Complete pre/post participation was required; individual reasons for missing test participation are not reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Participants (allocation counts); p. 12, Data analysis, first paragraph (complete-case rule and retained counts); p. 6, Fig. 1 shows the procedure but no attrition breakdown.

confirmed.statement: The 185 test papers and 3,010 coded entries are records of repeated tests and questions, not unique participants. Scores were calculated for each student, so 89 denotes people rather than ideas, ratings, sessions, or pairs of different people.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, scoring explanation and Table 4 (multiple questions from student S2); p. 12, Data analysis, first and third paragraphs; p. 13, Table 5.

confirmed.statement: Of 93 questionnaires collected, 7 were excluded for missing data or straightlining in either scale, leaving 86 respondents: 42 chatbot and 44 search-engine students. The two scales appeared in the same questionnaire and do not represent separate participant samples.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Questionnaires on cognitive load and technology acceptance, final sentence, and Data analysis, first paragraph; p. 14, Differences in cognitive load and technology acceptance, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The 30-student pilot was explicitly outside the main study sample and tested the research instruments. It is not added to S1 or treated as another randomized AI comparison.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5?6, Implementation procedure; p. 9, Problem posing ability tests, pilot-test discussion.

confirmed.statement: The three thematic inquiry rounds and pre/post tests belong to the same two classes in one experiment. Repeated phases do not supply additional independent samples; per-topic ENA participant counts are not stated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Implementation procedure and Fig. 1; pp. 12?13, ENA methods and Results RQ2; p. 14, Figs. 3?4.

confirmed.statement: No cross-paper reuse of participants is reported in the supplied document. The form appropriately records this as not stated; absence of overlap cannot be established from the paper.
confirmed.locator: Entire supplied document, PDF pp. 1?22 / markdown lines 1?817; especially pp. 5?6, Participants and Implementation procedure, and p. 19, Data availability.

confirmed.statement: The supplied 22-page PDF ends with references and contains no appended or embedded supplementary files. Additional files 1 and 2 are referenced but were not found among matching local files; urllib requests to the DOI, Springer, and SpringerOpen article pages all failed with WinError 10013, so their contents remain unverified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, reference to Additional file 1; p. 13, references to Additional file 2; p. 19, Supplementary Information; pp. 19?22, references; local-file and named-source retrieval checks during this audit.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds for S1 alone: 45+44=89 analyzed people across its two randomly allocated classes, exceeding 50 without adding the pilot or repeated records.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Participants; p. 12, Data analysis; p. 13, Table 5; creativity-codebook.md sections 3 and 7.

summary: The PDF supports 97 students assigned (48 chatbot, 49 search) and 89 analyzed (45 and 44) in one class-randomized study. No participant-count error was found, and criterion 2 holds.
